title: Ekphrasis: Contextual Corners — Reading Dossier (Lina Gopal, 2027-06)
body:
One-page skimmable dossier for follow-ups and short experiments. Quick riffs + concrete next steps. Mostly free-form notes to help plan a small sprint (2–3 days) to probe context-handling strategies on Redwood inference runtime.

Housekeeping: goal is to capture interesting ideas from this week’s pile: latency-vs-cost tradeoffs for different caching regimes, stability of low-bit quantization under long KV lifetimes, and compositional effects when retrieval and prefix caches both hit.

Papers / posts (short takeaways):
1) Latent-prefix cache (paper A) — idea: store a compressed latent prefix instead of raw KV to reduce memory + traffic. Takeaway: compression helps when prefix reuse is high; decoder recomposition adds small compute overhead. Hypothesis: on our runtime, decompression cost may be amortized by reduced GPU memory pressure enabling larger batch sizes.

2) Mosaic cache / KV sharding (paper B) — shard KV across hosts with lightweight routing. Takeaway: complexity in routing + staleness management; useful for very long sessions where full KV is >1GB. For Dedicated pools, consider an intra-pod shard layout to avoid cross-pod network hop.

3) Chunked attention + interleaved KV eviction (blog/post C) — pragmatic heuristics for eviction based on recency+semantic importance. Takeaway: simple age-based eviction is surprisingly decent; semantic heuristics need a cheap scorer (dot product with last query embedding).

4) Quantization stability notes (paper D) — small top-k generation shifts when using 4-bit asymmetric quant; worst when combined with attention approximation. Takeaway: run small regression tests of end-to-end output (ROUGE/BLEU + custom hallucination probes) before rolling quant profile to production.

Conference snippets (internal):
- Panel on "Serving tradeoffs": everyone emphasizes observability + canarying. We should add a tiny canary prompt set that exercises long-context coherence and retrieval fallbacks.
- Demo: fallback-to-smaller-model-with-cache showed better UX than fallback-to-slower-model-no-cache. Good operational prior.

Concrete experiments (priority ordered):
A) Prefix-compression microbenchmark (2d): implement lightweight decompress step in a branch of cache-playground; measure per-token latency, memory, and throughput for seq lengths [512, 2k, 8k]. Metrics: p50/p95 token latency, GPU memory usage, tokens/sec, and end-to-end perf on a 4k prefix reuse workload.
B) Shard-locality test (1d): simulate KV shards within a single Dedicated pod vs cross-pod; measure tail latency and network bytes.
C) Quantized-regression (1d): run T0-style prompts comparing fp16 baseline vs 4-bit profile + chunked attention; compute simple hallucination probe (fact-check exactness) and delta in log-prob distributions for target tokens.
D) Canary prompt set (ongoing): assemble ~30 prompts that target hallucination, repetition, long-coherence. Put behind a roll gate in Console (low friction).

Notes on instrumentation: need token-level tracing + provenance of which cache layer served each token. Tag traces with model-variant, cache-hit-type (prefix, kv-local, kv-remote), quant-profile. Add a small analytics view: hit-rate vs tail-latency heatmap.

Open questions / risks:
- Decompression cost might blow up p95 on small payloads — need to test worst-case.
- Sharded KV raises consistency complexity; acceptable for best-effort retrieval but not for exact-state workloads.
- Quant + attention approx may create subtle instability; guard with regression gates.

Actions (next 7 days):
- Kenji: spin up cache-playground branch + small script for latent-prefix compress/decompress (due 2027-06-18).
- Mira: assemble canary prompt set and lightweight scoring rubric (due 2027-06-18).
- Lina (me): wire ephemeral trace tags in local test harness and draft an ops note for Console small viz (due 2027-06-20).

Misc scratch ideas:
- Try semantic eviction using hashed buckets of last-k query embeddings (cheap incremental dot prod).
- Explore hybrid fallback: first try quantized model with cache; if hallucination score > threshold, refire with fp16 model without cache.

References & quick links: embedded in linked_artifacts above. Keep this file as a rolling log; will move polished docs to shared_drives/product or confluence when we have a clear decision.

Short summary to paste in standup: testing latent-prefix compression + shard-locality hypotheses to reduce memory and tail-latency for long-session workloads; building a 30-prompt canary to catch quantization-induced regressions.
